reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates N-doping forming M–N bonds and a Pt-rich shell in an HEA catalyst, enhancing durability under HDV conditions for the ORR. However, it does not address automotive exhaust oxidation reactions, poisoning by H2O/NO, or low-temperature activity below 150 °C, leaving several key premises unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Nitrogen doping of a multi-principal-element alloy can form multiple stable M–N bonds and a Pt-rich surface
M–N bonds and a Pt-rich shell enhance catalytic activity and durability
These structural features resist poisoning by H2O and NO
